pages.title: The Pot Is a Black Box
pages.text: A ceramic melting pot melts without a skim, without flux and open to the fire, so it holds its melt down to **10% slag** no matter how clean the charge was: nothing poured out of a pot is ever pure metal, and it costs you a tenth of the charge as fire loss.$p$pIt is still forgiving: the ratio bands are wide, so a pot pour becomes Flawed metal rather than junk.

pages.title: Pouring Out of a Pot
pages.text: Right-click the pot while its contents are molten to open it, and put a mold into the slots there. While the bath holds liquid the pot is not an inventory any more, so the same gesture does not show you the four item slots.$p$pMelted parts and ingots keep their dirt when you re-melt them, so a pot's output stays dirty through the loop until it is skimmed in a crucible.

pages.title: The Crucible Is the Refinery
pages.text: Only a crucible can be skimmed and fluxed, so it is the one object that turns ore or pot metal into clean metal. Everything else in this book happens there.$p$pPicked up, a crucible keeps what its melt was made of, so a flawed pour in a chest does not forget its own composition.
